title: Eve Legal Reviews
summary: Eve Legal offers strong downstream AI tools for plaintiff firms, but its medical record retrieval capabilities and pricing details are more limited than its analysis suite. See how Codes Health's dedicated retrieval and human-verified analysis compare.
body_text: Eve Legal has emerged as one of the most talked-about AI platforms in plaintiff litigation, reaching a $1 billion-plus valuation and serving over 1,200 plaintiff firms. But for law firms evaluating legal AI tools, the question isn't just whether Eve Legal works; it's whether the platform addresses the actual bottlenecks slowing down your cases. For many personal injury and mass tort practices, a persistent challenge is getting complete medical records in the first place. This review examines Eve Legal's capabilities, reported strengths and limitations, and where plaintiff firms may want to pair it with a dedicated retrieval platform like Codes Health to address the upstream part of the workflow. Key Takeaways Eve Legal doesn't publicly document a full-service, end-to-end medical record retrieval offering comparable to a specialist retrieval platform, though its current agents can assist with requesting and following up on records. Eve now supports much larger document uploads than earlier reviews suggested: the company states it can process files with thousands of pages and automatically splits PDFs of up to 10,000 pages. Eve reports a 4.9/5 rating on G2, based on the rating displayed when this article was reviewed, and states it supports more than 200,000 cases, though its materials have described that figure both as annual volume and as active cases. Eve doesn't publish general platform subscription tiers, though its medical-malpractice page discloses roughly $350 per case for chronology work in that specific context; broader platform pricing requires a quote. Codes Health documents multi-channel retrieval, Missing Record Review, and pre-submission authorization checking, typically delivering complete records in a couple of weeks. Firms can use the two platforms together, with Codes Health handling retrieval and Eve supporting downstream drafting and case work, though no adoption data establishes how common that combination currently is. What Eve Legal Offers Plaintiff Firms Eve Legal positions itself as a full-lifecycle AI platform for plaintiff litigation. The company has raised a total of $164 million in funding, including a $14 million seed round, a $47 million Series A, and a $103 million Series B that valued the company at more than $1 billion. Eve reports that its platform supports more than 200,000 cases, though its public materials have described that figure both as annual case volume and as active cases on the platform. Core Capabilities Eve Legal's platform includes: AI voice intake : 24/7 automated intake in more than 28 languages with lead scoring and qualification Medical chronology generation : AI-powered summaries are generally produced in 15 to 20 minutes after records are available to the platform Demand letter drafting : Automated demand packages that use firm templates, tone, and writing preferences Discovery support : Document organization, interrogatory and discovery-response drafting, and exhibit assembly Built-in legal research : Case law, statutes, regulations, medical literature, and other research sources Case management integrations : Eve documents integrations with systems including Filevine, Clio, Litify, SmartAdvocate, and Growpath; its intake product also works with CRMs such as Clio and MyCase Where Eve Legal Shines Eve's official G2 listing includes customer feedback praising the platform's "customer support team has been consistently excellent." Other reviewers describe the platform as useful across case evaluation, legal research, and day-to-day document review, note that it helps attorneys work through documents and facts more quickly, and highlight that its drafting adapts to a firm's preferred tone and format for demands, discovery documents, and similar filings. For firms that already have reliable medical record retrieval processes in place, Eve Legal offers substantial workflow automation for everything that happens after records arrive. Eve Legal Limitations: What to Confirm Before Signing Alongside its strengths, a few areas are worth confirming directly with Eve during evaluation. Document Upload and Processing Older reviews reported lower upload limits, around 200 PDF pages, that required manual document splitting. Eve's current materials describe considerably higher capacity: the company says it can process files containing thousands of pages and automatically splits PDFs of up to 10,000 pages, with exceptionally large matters uploaded in batches. Firms that evaluated Eve some time ago should confirm current limits rather than relying on older reviews. Medical Record Retrieval Scope Eve doesn't publicly document a full-service, end-to-end medical record retrieval offering comparable to a specialist retrieval platform's HIE, custodian, provider-network, and traditional outreach model. That said, Eve states that its current agents can assist with requesting records, and its communications agent can follow up on outstanding requests. Firms should confirm the scope of that functionality directly with Eve, since it's less clear whether it's positioned as a complete substitute for a dedicated retrieval workflow. Where retrieval remains a firm's primary bottleneck, that's a gap worth discussing directly with Eve or addressing through a dedicated retrieval vendor: Record retrieval bottlenecks can delay case progression Incomplete records can contribute to missed diagnoses or treatment gaps Authorization errors can cause provider rejections Staff time spent chasing records can limit case capacity Pricing Transparency Eve doesn't publish general platform subscription tiers and directs firms to contact sales. It does disclose roughly $350 per case for a specific medical-malpractice chronology use case on its website, but firms need a customized quote to understand broader platform pricing and how it compares with other legal AI products. Implementation Timeline Eve states that most firms are fully operational within 90 days, with timing depending on integrations, templates, workflows, training, and firm size. Users also report that upfront configuration, teaching the system firm preferences, and setting up templates takes meaningful onboarding effort even after go-live. The Medical Record Retrieval Question For firms where medical record retrieval is a bottleneck, that's worth weighing separately from Eve's downstream analysis and drafting strengths, since even sophisticated AI analysis can't work with records a firm doesn't have yet. Why Retrieval Matters Common retrieval challenges include: Authorization errors causing rejections: Missing patient signatures Unclear expiration dates Missing consent language for sensitive record categories Misspellings in patient or provider names Missing dates of service Authorization errors can force a request to be corrected and resubmitted, delaying the applicable provider response period. Under federal HIPAA, covered entities generally have 30 calendar days to act on a valid request, subject to a possible extension, while some states impose shorter deadlines in certain circumstances. Missing records creating trial risks: Treatment gaps that opposing counsel may surface at deposition Diagnostic records from facilities that the plaintiff forgot to mention Prior condition documentation affecting causation arguments Billing records needed for accurate damage calculations Coordination overhead with multiple vendors: Managing separate relationships with retrieval and analysis vendors Ensuring data formats work between systems Determining accountability when records arrive late or incomplete Handling separate invoicing from multiple service providers How Codes Health Approaches Retrieval For firms where medical record retrieval is the primary case progression barrier, Codes Health focuses specifically on that part of the workflow. Complete Record Retrieval Codes Health retrieves medical and billing records through multiple channels: Claims clearinghouses Custodian integrations Proprietary provider networks Traditional fax and phone retrieval Patient upload portals Codes Health typically delivers complete records in a couple of weeks, using Missing Record Review and completeness verification to identify and pursue potential gaps before delivery, rather than treating every matter as guaranteed to capture every possible record on the first pass. Missing Record Detection Codes Health's AI cross-references patient medical history to flag documentation gaps before trial preparation. This is intended to reduce surprises when opposing counsel raises records a firm's team never obtained. Authorization Error Prevention AI pre-submission checking reviews authorization requests before they go to providers, flagging: Misspellings in patient or provider names Missing signatures or unclear wet signatures Dates of service errors Missing consent language for sensitive records Expiration date issues This addresses a leading cause of denied or delayed record requests and is intended to help prevent the kind of rejections that can add weeks to a case timeline. Human-Verified AI Insights Codes Health states that its AI-generated case insights are verified by medical and legal experts as a standard feature, pairing automated extraction with human review. General AI tools like ChatGPT are not reliable for litigation-grade medical record analysis, since they aren't built to parse dense, inconsistent clinical documentation across providers or reliably tie findings back to source records. Codes Health's platform is purpose-built for this task. Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and product capabilities, helping the platform keep evolving to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. The platform offers flat-fee pricing, and for high-volume firms, Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other case management or medical software. Streamlined Vendor Management Rather than coordinating separate retrieval and analysis vendors, Codes Health provides both capabilities in a single relationship, which can reduce coordination overhead. When to Choose Eve Legal vs. Codes Health These platforms address different parts of the plaintiff litigation workflow. The right choice depends on where your firm's bottlenecks actually exist. Choose Eve Legal When: You have reliable medical record retrieval already solved, whether through internal staff, an effective vendor, or Eve's own request and follow-up agents You need full-lifecycle automation from intake through discovery 24/7 AI voice intake with lead scoring fits your client acquisition model Your primary pain point is downstream document drafting rather than record gathering You want built-in legal research integrated with case analysis Choose Codes Health When: Medical record retrieval delays are your primary case progression bottleneck Authorization rejections and incomplete records create trial risks You want a vendor focused specifically on retrieval and AI-powered analysis Missing record detection before trial preparation is a priority You want human-verified insights included as a standard feature Consider Both When: Firms can use the platforms together, with Codes Health handling retrieval and Eve supporting downstream analysis and casework. The tools are technically complementary, though there's no reliable adoption data establishing how many firms currently combine them. Integration and Implementation Considerations Eve Legal Integrations Eve documents integrations with Filevine, Clio, Litify, SmartAdvocate, and Growpath, plus telephony connections to Zoom Contact Center, Dialpad, and RingCentral for its AI intake features. Eve supports integrations with several case management and communications systems; firms needing a custom integration should confirm technical options directly with Eve, since no public API documentation was identified. Codes Health Integrations Codes Health announced a partnership with Filevine on July 13, 2026, bringing medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine platform. The company also builds custom integrations for high-volume customers with CRM platforms and medical software systems. Implementation Considerations Setup timelines vary by firm size, integrations, data migration, templates, and workflow configuration, so treat any specific estimate as a starting point rather than a guarantee: Adding Eve Legal to an existing workflow : Eve states that most firms are fully operational within 90 days, depending on integration and training needs Adding Codes Health for retrieval : Timing depends on case volume and provider complexity; one customer case study described a CRM integration completed within a couple of weeks, though this isn't a universal benchmark Running both platforms together : The general handoff is straightforward in concept, Codes Health delivers records, Eve analyzes them, but firms should confirm data-format compatibility between the two systems during setup The Bottom Line on Eve Legal Eve Legal has earned a strong reputation for downstream workflow automation. The platform's reported 4.9/5 G2 rating, 1,200-plus firm customer base, and unicorn valuation reflect genuine value for firms whose primary need is analyzing and acting on records they already have. For practices where getting complete medical records remains a bottleneck, that's worth addressing directly, either by confirming the scope of Eve's own request and follow-up agents or by pairing Eve with a dedicated retrieval vendor. The upload-limit improvements narrow one older gap, but pricing transparency for the broader platform is still limited to a quote-based process. Plaintiff firms evaluating AI platforms should assess where their workflows break down: If records arrive quickly and completely, Eve Legal offers powerful downstream automation If retrieval delays, authorization errors, and incomplete records slow case progression, addressing that upstream problem directly, whether through Eve's own agents or a dedicated vendor, is worth prioritizing If both matter, stacking Codes Health for retrieval with Eve Legal for analysis is one way to address the fuller workflow Frequently Asked Questions Does Eve Legal retrieve medical records, or do I need a separate service? Eve doesn't publicly document a full-service, end-to-end medical record retrieval offering comparable to a specialist retrieval platform. Its current agents can assist with requesting and following up on records, so firms should confirm the scope of that functionality directly with Eve. Firms with heavier retrieval needs often use a dedicated vendor like Codes Health alongside Eve's analysis and drafting tools. What are the document upload limits in Eve Legal? Eve's current materials state that it can process files containing thousands of pages and automatically splits PDFs of up to 10,000 pages, a significant increase from the roughly 200-page limits reported in older reviews. Firms evaluating Eve based on older information should confirm current limits directly. Can I use Codes Health and Eve Legal together? Yes. Some firms use Codes Health for medical record retrieval, typically complete records in a couple of weeks with missing record detection and authorization error prevention, then feed those records into Eve Legal for downstream workflow automation. This combines an upstream retrieval step with Eve's downstream analysis and drafting capabilities. What practice areas does Eve Legal support? Eve Legal supports plaintiff-side practices, including personal injury, workers' compensation, medical malpractice, labor and employment, mass torts, and Social Security disability. The platform is designed for plaintiff firms rather than defense-side work, employer-side policy review, or corporate legal departments. How does Codes Health's verification process work? Codes Health states that AI-generated case insights are verified by medical and legal experts as a standard feature. This combines automated AI extraction with human review, intended to address concerns about AI errors or misinterpretations that would otherwise require additional attorney review time.

title: How to Pay 3,500+ Get-Out-the-Vote Workers in One Day
summary: How DJs at the Polls paid 3,500+ get-out-the-vote workers with Dots: $4.9M in payouts, a 96% success rate, and 2,184 1099s filed automatically.
body_text: DJs at the Polls hires thousands of DJs to lift turnout on Election Day, then pays them all within hours. Here's how they moved $4.9M to 3,500+ workers through Dots, at a 96% payout success rate. The short version Who: DJs at the Polls , a national nonpartisan get-out-the-vote nonprofit that places DJs at polling sites to boost turnout. Challenge: Pay thousands of independent DJs across the country accurately and fast, with 1099 tax compliance, in a single Election Day. Solution: Dots' payouts platform, letting each DJ pick their own payout method and get paid on the rail they already use. Results: $4.9M+ processed across 6,800+ payouts to 3,559 DJs at a 96% success rate, including $1.7M to 1,800+ DJs in a single day . About DJs at the Polls Founder Anton Moore, a longtime radio and TV producer who also runs an anti-gun-violence nonprofit in the citym had a simple idea: voting shouldn't feel like a chore. It started with a single DJ at one polling place in South Philadelphia. It worked, and not just anecdotally. A 2022 randomized controlled trial in Philadelphia found that turnout rose about 3% at polling places with a DJ. That evidence turned a local idea into a national, nonpartisan movement. By the 2024 general election, DJs at the Polls had grown from that one DJ to more than 3,000 of them, spread across nearly 6,000 polling sites in 11 states. The Challenge: How Do You Pay Thousands of Get-Out-The-Vote Workers at Once? Mission success created an operational problem. Every one of those DJs is an independent contractor who expects to be paid quickly after their shift, and the whole workforce is deployed on a single day. Each DJ is compensated $500 per shift (up to $1,000 for a full day) and paid in two parts: the bulk up front, with the remainder released within 48 hours once they submit a post-election survey. That structure alone means roughly two payments per DJ, thousands of them concentrated around one date. It's a payments problem most nonprofits never have to solve, and it's the same one facing any civic campaign that pays canvassers, poll workers, or field staff: onboard thousands of gig workers, collect their tax information, and disburse thousands of payments in a compressed window — without a large finance team, and without making anyone wait days for a check. The Solution: Let Every DJ Get Paid Their Way With Dots, DJs at the Polls sends each performer a payout and lets them choose how to receive it — no forced bank onboarding, no chasing account numbers. Payees land on the rail they already use, and the results show why that matters: nearly half of all payouts (49%) went to instant peer-to-peer apps , such as Venmo, PayPal, and Cash App, rather than a traditional bank transfer. How DJs Chose to Get Paid 50% chose to get paid via bank transfers, 23% via Venmo, 20% by Paypal, and others by Cash App, Amazon gift cards, and Airtm. That spread is the whole point. Force everyone onto one rail and you lose the DJs who don't have, or don't want to share, a bank account. Offer seven and completion stays high while support tickets stay low. Dots also handles the compliance layer nonprofits dread: collecting W-9s and generating tax forms, so obligations don't pile up for January. Across these cycles, Dots auto-filed 2,000+ 1099s on the organization's behalf, without any manual collection or year-end scramble. The Results Overall, $4.9 million was paid out through Dots, across 3,500+ DJs and nearly 7,000 total payouts processed. Additionally, $1.7 million was sent to approximately 1,800 DJs in a single day on the peak payout day after the 2024 general election. The November 2024 cycle alone accounted for 6,000+ payouts to more than 3,300 DJs totaling $3.58M . That's the kind of concentrated, high-volume disbursement that breaks manual processes but is a routine day for an automated payouts platform. And it didn't stop after the general: DJs at the Polls has kept using Dots through 2025 and into 2026 for primaries and local elections, paying hundreds more DJs each cycle. “We recruited 4,000 DJs from neighborhoods that they actually live in. We compensate $500 a shift to get the word out about voting.” — Anton Moore, Founder & Co-Director, DJs at the Polls (The Philly Download, Nov. 2024) How to Pay Canvassers, Poll Workers, and Field Staff at Scale If your organization pays people to power democracy, such as canvassers, poll workers, phone-bankers, DJs, drivers, field staff, you face the same math DJs at the Polls did: a lot of independent workers, a hard deadline, and real tax obligations. The playbook that worked for them is the same one that works for any get-out-the-vote or civic campaign: onboard workers fast with no forced bank setup, let each person pick the payout method they already use, disburse thousands of payments at once, and let the platform collect W-9s and file 1099s automatically. That's what Dots is built for. Paying canvassers, poll workers, or field staff this cycle? Get set up before your next deadline and pay everyone instantly, on the rail they prefer, fully 1099-compliant. Platforms like Dots let a campaign send each worker a payout and have them choose how to receive itm Venmo, PayPal, Cash App, instant debit, or bank transfer, while automatically collecting W-9s and generating 1099s. How fast can get-out-the-vote workers be paid? On instant rails, funds arrive in seconds to minutes. Does Dots handle 1099 tax compliance for campaign workers? Yes.
